verdict.rationale: ADK documents packaging agents into containers that run in any container environment, including a one-command local Docker deploy. It names an option for running offline or in systems with no connection to Google Cloud, and it supports locally running models, so agents need not depend on Google's platform or model APIs. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of fully disconnected operation, detailed docs on which option the offline guidance refers to and on self-hosted replacements for managed services (sessions, storage).

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can run my agents entirely on my own infrastructure with no dependence on the vendor's platform

citations.quote: You can manually package your Agent into a container image and then run it in any environment that supports container images.
This is a good option if you prefer to run offline or disconnected, or otherwise in a system that has no connection to Google Cloud.

Deploying the Agent Locally with Docker Container:

adk deploy docker --with_ui <agent-folder>
we provide adapters that let you connect with many other models and model providers, including locally running models.
